📌 Tehran, IRNA – The daily report provides a summary of the violations committed by the occupation forces since the ceasefire agreement came into force, documenting these through figures and field developments.

The report reviews the numbers of martyrs and wounded, details of armed incidents, and an assessment of the flow of humanitarian and commercial assistance. It does not reiterate previous violations that remain unresolved to date, particularly the breaches of the agreed withdrawal lines, the imposition of armed control over additional areas outside the scope of the agreement, amounting to approximately 34 square kilometers, non-compliance with the humanitarian protocol, and the obstruction of urgent infrastructure repairs, including electricity, water, and sewage networks.
​
It also notes the prevention of the entry of heavy machinery required for infrastructure works, the continued exposure of detainees to serious violations, including torture and inhuman treatment, and the ongoing lack of clarity regarding the fate of the missing, all constituting clear violations of the ceasefire agreement and international humanitarian law.
​
These accumulated violations are added to the ongoing daily violations, as follows:
​
Fifth: Humanitarian, Commercial, and Fuel Trucks
​
The occupation authorities have failed to comply with the provisions of the agreement related to the entry of aids, which stipulate the entry of 600 trucks per day, including 50 fuel trucks. They continue to provide misleading figures to the mediators and refuse to submit to independent international monitoring.
​
Field data confirm that what has actually entered does not exceed 36% of the total number of trucks agreed upon. The most serious violation concerns the entry of fuel, as the quantity allowed to enter did not exceed 15.6%, underscoring a deliberate obstruction of recovery efforts and the continuation of basic services in the Gaza Strip.
​
Sixth: Violations at the Rafah Crossing
​
The Israeli occupation forces continue to violate the ceasefire agreement by obstructing the normal operation of the Rafah Crossing and failing to adhere to the humanitarian protocol. This is carried out through the imposition of arbitrary and degrading procedures and a severe reduction in the number of permitted crossings, including humanitarian and medical cases whose passage was agreed to be facilitated. These practices constitute a clear breach of the agreement and of the provisions of international humanitarian law. The table below illustrates the continued nature of these violations up to Friday, 11 September 2026.
​
All in all, the data demonstrates that the violations committed by the occupation forces constitute a continuous and systematic pattern that has struck at the core of the agreement and stripped its procedures of their practical substance. These findings underscore the urgent need for serious international action to ensure an end to the violations and the protection of civilians.
​

🔊 Iran urges enhanced cooperation with Uzbekistan in tourism and cultural heritage

📌 Tehran – IRNA – The Minister of Cultural Heritage, Tourism, and Handicrafts says Iran is ready to define a new horizon in tourism and cultural heritage with Uzbekistan.

In a meeting with Uzbekistan Ambassador to Tehran, Fariddin Nasriev, Seyed Reza Salehi Amiri stressed the need to leverage shared civilizational commonalities and take practical steps toward private-sector cooperation, as well as facilitating flight and visa mechanisms.
​
The two sides also discussed enhancing cultural exchanges, reviving the historical ties of the Silk Road, and developing the tourism industry.
​
Salehi Amiri emphasized convergence in the restoration of historical monuments and the revival of the Silk Road’s cultural identity as a component of civilizational convergence, stating that the historical and architectural patterns of Uzbekistan’s cities of Bukhara and Samarkand, alongside Iran’s city of Isfahan, are a brilliant reflection of shared cultural and Islamic heritage.
​
The Uzbek ambassador, for his part, said that given the many cultural attractions in Iranian cities such as Isfahan, Shiraz, and Mashhad, current direct flights are operating at full capacity, and Tashkent is seriously pursuing the launch of more regular weekly flights.
